name: manual_63c3a8
claim: When fixing a test to route through a real function instead of a synthetic fixture, verify every downstream assertion's indexing/shape assumptions too, not just the input construction — changing what data flows in without checking what the assertions expect out leaves a differently-broken test

decisions.notes: Fixed a plan's test to call the real redact_portal_status_payload() instead of a hand-rolled dict (closing the exact gap that hid a production bug), but left the assertion indexing into the wrapped dict shape as if it were still a plain list -- seen_by_publisher[0]['agents'][0] raised KeyError against the real dict-wrapped {'agents': [...], 'count': n} shape. An independent Codex GPT-5.5 pass caught it after the plan had already been marked APPROVED by 3 prior review phases (CEO, Eng, DX), none of which caught this because they were focused on the fixture's input construction, not the assertions consuming the corrected shape.
